newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROY MAKES TRIUMPHANT RETURN TO MONTREAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROY MAKES TRIUMPHANT RETURN TO MONTREAL.

text.p: Patrick Roy made a triumphant return to Montreal as Adam Deadmarsh had two goals and an assist to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 7-3 victory over the Canadiens Wednesday.
Roy was cheered wildly by a sellout crowd at the Molson Centre in his first game in Montreal since December 2, 1995, when he was pulled after allowing nine goals in a 11-1 loss to Detroit.
The All-Star goaltender demanded a trade and was dealt to Colorado, where he led the Avalanche to the Stanley Cup championship last spring.
Roy made 34 saves and received prolonged ovations when he took the ice during warmups, when he led Colorado onto the ice for the start of the game and when he was announced in the starting lineup.
"It was difficult for me to concentrate and focus with all the cheering I got and with all the excitement in this city about me coming back," he said.
"The main objective was to win the game and we won it. I had to really concentrate out there."
The Avalanche made sure Roy's return was a successful one, driving his successor, Jocelyn Thibault, from the nets midway through the second period in building a five-goal lead.
"We knew it was a big, huge game for Patrick. I'm happy he did well," Deadmarsh said.
Colorado has won three straight and nine of its last 11.
Martin Rucinsky tallied twice for Montreal, which suffered its third straight home loss.

In Buffalo, Derek Plante had a goal and two assists and Dominik Hasek turned away 23 shots for his league-leading 33rd win as the Sabres stretched their home unbeaten streak to 11 games with a 4-2 victory over the reeling Pittsburgh Penguins.
Donald Audette, Dixon Ward and Alexei Zhitnik also tallied for Buffalo, 9-1-5 in its last 15 games and 7-0-4 in its last 11 at home.

The Sabres, who have won all three home meetings with the Penguins this season, already are one victory ahead of last season's total of 33. Buffalo leads Pittsburgh by 11 points in the Northeast Division.

At Florida, Nikolai Khabibulin needed just 14 saves for his fourth shutout of the season and Mike Gartner had a goal and an assist as the Phoenix Coyotes began a three-game road trip with a 3-0 blanking of the slumping Panthers.
Khabibulin was hardly tested over the final two periods, stopping all eight shots en route to his sixth career shutout.
"It was probably the easiest game I've ever had," he said.
Jeremy Roenick and Cliff Ronning also tallied for Phoenix, which won for the second time in six games.
In Dallas, Mike Modano scored his team-leading 28th goal and set up Jere Lehtinen's third-period insurance tally as the Stars won for the fifth time in six games, 3-2 over the St Louis Blues.
Modano and Lehtinen assisted on each other's goals and Todd Harvey also tallied for Dallas.
The victory extended the Stars' lead to six points over second-place Detroit in the Central Division.
In Hartford, Sean Burke stopped 28 shots for his second shutout in 12 days and his first career win over Calgary in the Whalers' 2-0 blanking of the Flames.

Keith Primeau had a shorthanded goal and Andrew Cassels added a power-play tally for the Whalers, who broke a three-game winless streak and climbed into a tie with Tampa Bay and Montreal for the final Eastern Conference playoff spot with 59 points.
Burke had been 0-11 against the Flames.

In Anaheim, Teemu Selanne scored twice and Paul Kariya had a goal and an assist as the Mighty Ducks extended their season-high unbeaten streak to six games (4-0-2) with a 4-1 victory over the Ottawa Senators.
Kariya's empty-net marker with four seconds left was his 100th career goal.
The Senators have lost four of their last five games.

In Philadelphia, Dave Andreychuk had a goal and an assist in a three-goal second period and Martin Brodeur stopped 26 shots, leading the red-hot New Jersey Devils to their fifth straight win, 3-1 over the Flyers.

Scott Niedermayer and Bill Guerin also scored for New Jersey, which has not lost since acquiring Doug Gilmour and Dave Ellett from Toronto on February 25. The Devils improved to 11-1-7 in their last 19 games and moved within four points of first-place Philadelphia in the Atlantic.
In Toronto, Mats Sundin scored his team-leading 35th goal with 88 seconds left to lift the Maple Leafs into a 4-4 tie with the Detroit Red Wings.
The tie extended Detroit's unbeaten streak to a season-high nine games (5-0-4).
In Vancouver, Esa Tikkanen scored a power-play goal with 3:06 left in regulation, lifting the Vancouver Canucks into a 1-1 tie with the Chicago Blackhawks.
The game remained scoreless until Chicago's Sergei Krivokrasov tallied with 5:56 remaining in regulation.
Corey Hirsch finished with 32 saves for Vancouver, 1-5-1 in its last seven games. Jeff Hackett stopped 28 shots for Chicago, which is 1-2-2 in its last five.
